objective: Filter unknown inputs by an exact primitive name while preserving distributive conditional result types.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Conditional aliases and predicate filtering remain current TypeScript tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Typed primitive selection is useful when adapting heterogeneous input.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Exact typeof semantics and ownership transfer to other narrowing helpers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Three finite primitive names keep this generic exercise focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Coercion, boxed primitive confusion or returning an input alias can break callers.

defects: The API unnecessarily required mutable inputs despite pure filtering.
Fresh results, all-match aliasing and exact number/boxed-value semantics were untested.
An implementation returning the input when every item matched passed the old cases.
rationale: Keep all three sound boards, accept an explicit loop as well as filter, and widen the input interface to readonly unknown[]. Define dense stable bounded inputs, exact typeof including NaN/infinities/signed zero and exclusion of boxed/null/Symbol/bigint/function values. Three runtime assertions inspect primitive classification, independent mutable all-match/empty results, frozen sources and1000 entries. Two static assertions exercise union-name results/never and a boolean-to-number mismatch. Target one constant-time typeof check per input; preserve duplicate/order semantics. The all-match alias adversary now fails without invalidating loop or guard-factory solutions.

objective: Return a precise nullable mutable index tuple without consuming a sorted readonly input.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Readonly arrays and nullable tuples are current TypeScript interfaces.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Locating a contiguous range is useful indexing work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Bounds, absent results and input preservation transfer to other search functions.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Finite sorted inputs keep the two-pointer practice within its intended level.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Consuming the input or reusing a mutable tuple silently corrupts later calls.

defects: The input/value numeric domain and comparison model were unstated.
No existing assertion inspected preserved input or result independence.
A correct-result implementation that popped the source still passed.
rationale: Retain the three correct scans and explicitly accept a valid binary lower/upper-bound alternative. Define bounded finite nondecreasing values, === equality including signed zero/fractions, exact null misses and fresh mutable result tuples. Three runtime assertions cover frozen empty/singleton/fraction/negative lists, source preservation and tuple independence, and1000 equal values with a miss. One positive static assertion confirms readonly input and mutable/narrowed tuple access; existing null and wrong-element negatives remain. Authored O(n) worst-case goal permits better logarithmic search; no binary-search-only requirement is imposed.

objective: Interleave two generic readonly lists while retaining opaque item identity and fresh output.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Shared generic type parameters and readonly list inputs remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Interleaving independent ordered streams is practical collection work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Opaque references, falsy items and unequal input lengths transfer to merge helpers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One index per list provides a clear foundational traversal objective.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Cloning arbitrary items can erase identity or change non-record data.

defects: The untyped starter generated avoidable implicit-any errors.
The same-kind wording omitted valid explicitly chosen union element types.
Old primitive-only tests accepted shallow-copying every object item.
Empty-result ownership, aliased list inputs and opaque values were not covered.
rationale: Give the starter the stated generic readonly signature and describe one shared T, including explicit unions. Keep all valid boards and an independent index-loop alternative. Four runtime assertions cover frozen objects/functions/Symbols/arrays/null/undefined by identity, fresh empty and one-sided results, repeated/aliased inputs and2000 output positions. A static explicit-union example complements the retained mixed-inference rejection. Define independent O(n + m) dimensions rather than a fake quadratic input model; its estimate stays unknown/base25 under #419. Dense stable arrays bound the exercise; no arbitrary sparse-array equivalence is claimed.

objective: Memoize one-argument callbacks by Map equality within one run while retaining the inferred output type.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Conditional infer and Map membership are current TypeScript/JavaScript tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Avoiding repeated callback work is a practical cache use case.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Undefined hits, key equality and cache lifetime transfer to other memoizers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A single numeric argument keeps the intermediate generic cache bounded.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: False cache misses or shared per-run state can duplicate side effects or return stale references.

defects: Junior used an object cache despite the Map teaching objective.
The brief did not specify NaN/signed-zero equality, undefined hits or per-run lifetime.
Callbacks with missing results, exact call semantics, throw order and opaque identity lacked coverage.
The get-is-undefined cache-miss adversary passed all original cases.
rationale: Rewrite junior to a local Map and make all boards accept readonly inputs. Explain has rather than value truthiness/nullish detection. Five runtime assertions inspect undefined/null/false/zero cache hits, NaN and signed-zero first-input semantics, plain one-argument call order and independent runs, immediate exception propagation and1000 inputs/ten distinct keys. Two static assertions preserve readonly opaque outputs/Promise result types and reject Output<number> as never. Promise values remain opaque, not awaited. State O(n) average bookkeeping with constant-average Map operations and explicitly exclude callback work; this is not a total-time promise for arbitrary fn. Normalize target wording so the existing authored-goal parser recognizes it.

objective: Build ordered duplicate-preserving tags with a generic template-literal return shape.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Template literal types and contextual string construction remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Typed labels and stable identifiers are useful presentation adapters.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Type-shape versus runtime validation and ordered duplicates transfer to other serializers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded integer interpolation keeps the foundational literal-type objective focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Nonfinite numbers can violate the advertised string shape; deduplication silently drops requested labels.

defects: The number[] signature did not explain the supported numeric domain of a template shape.
Readonly inputs, negative/signed-zero formatting and duplicate preservation were implicit.
A Set-based deduplicating mapper passed all old unique-ID examples.
rationale: Preserve the three sound boards, widen ids to readonly, and accept an independent Array.from mapping. Bound ids to finite safe integers within1e9 so ordinary number interpolation fits Tag; explicitly exclude nonfinite runtime numbers rather than adding new validation behavior. Three runtime assertions cover duplicate/negative/zero/Unicode-dashed-prefix formatting, fresh mutable repeated/empty outputs and1000 IDs with the100-unit prefix bound. Two static assertions cover union prefixes/readonly IDs and a malformed suffix. Target O(n) under these fixed text bounds; the type is a shape rather than a validator. This exercise does not implement actual globally numbered shark profile names.
